narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The paper stays the same, but a famous name changes how people read it.

direction.delivery: Conversational and immediately clear; give light emphasis to “paper stays the same”. Sound interested in the question, not as if revealing a secret.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Borrowed Credibility examines how reputation travels through science, sometimes faster than evidence.

direction.delivery: Natural and precise; give light emphasis to “faster than evidence”. Keep the thought easy to follow; no grand or solemn delivery.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A manuscript reaches busy editors who cannot check everything in equal depth.

direction.delivery: Natural and precise; give light emphasis to “cannot check everything”. Keep the thought easy to follow; no grand or solemn delivery.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Names, universities, and journals help them decide where to spend their attention.

direction.delivery: Natural and precise; give light emphasis to “where to spend their attention”. Keep the thought easy to follow; no grand or solemn delivery.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those shortcuts can be useful, yet they do not change the experiment behind the paper.

direction.delivery: Natural and precise; give light emphasis to “do not change the experiment”. Keep the thought easy to follow; no grand or solemn delivery.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows what happens when attention brings citations, funding, and still more attention.

direction.delivery: Natural and precise; give light emphasis to “still more attention”. Let concern come from the situation; no alarm or dramatic drop in pitch.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks how research can earn trust without making every reader start from zero.

direction.delivery: Natural and precise; give light emphasis to “without making every reader start from zero”. Keep the thought easy to follow; no grand or solemn delivery.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: When should a respected name give way to evidence?

direction.delivery: Warm, unhurried closing; give light emphasis to “give way to evidence”. Keep the thought easy to follow; no grand or solemn delivery.
